parsed.why: No criminalisation and civil partnerships, but documented hate-crime impunity (court found violations), no gender-identity anti-discrimination protection, and a cleric's hostile rhetoric. Trans-specific exposure is thin; visitor-facing restrictions undocumented. Reduced band, lower end.

Marriage equality, self-ID since 2017, broad protections, but a 2024 mob attack on trans people with later arrests, documented 2013 police stops of trans sex workers, weak comparative survey findings, and a recurring prison-placement practice that defaulted to male facilities until on-request transfer. Elevated band.

Sections 153/156 criminalise same-sex conduct, enforced; a trans woman was sentenced to eight years in a men's prison; documented police arbitrary arrest and assault of trans people; state-linked hostility; moratorium workarounds. Severe.

No criminalisation, anti-discrimination law covering gender identity, but documented police assault in custody probe, pride violence, 20+ attacks on an LGBT centre unsanctioned, and prison searches requiring recommendation. Recurring unremedied hostility, with state-linked police exposure. High band, upper edge.

Permissive framework: self-declaration, hate-crime aggravation, facilities protected, conversion therapy banned. But a March 2026 parliamentary vote backs reimposing medical requirements, and a rollback is pending. Future-facing risk tempers the current reduced-risk rating.
